slides.title: Welcome to JSX!
slides.content: In this lesson, we'll explore JSX - a key concept in React that allows us to write HTML-like syntax directly in our JavaScript code. Get ready to dive into the world of React and see how JSX simplifies our coding experience!
slides.visualDescription: A captivating image of a React logo integrating JSX elements, showcasing the relationship between React and JSX.

slides.title: What is JSX?
slides.content: JSX, standing for JavaScript XML, allows developers to write HTML structures in the same file as JavaScript code. It combines the best of both worlds, enhancing code readability and expressiveness.
keyPoints: Makes HTML-like syntax accessible in JS
slides.visualDescription: A diagram illustrating JSX syntax with labels showing how JSX translates to respective JavaScript function calls, making the connection clear.

slides.title: JSX Syntax Basics
slides.content: JSX looks similar to HTML but comes with some differences. Remember, all JSX tags must be closed, whether they're single or double tags. Let's explore these syntax rules in detail!
slides.visualDescription: An infographic displaying key JSX syntax rules with examples to clarify each point, using visuals to highlight differences from HTML.

slides.title: Writing JSX with Components
slides.content: Let’s see how JSX works within a React component. By writing JSX directly into our components, we can easily create dynamic UIs. Check out this simple example of a functional component!
slides.visualDescription: Code snippets highlighting a functional component and its JSX usage, presented in a code block format for clarity.

slides.title: JSX in Action
slides.content: Now let’s look at a practical application of JSX in a React project. We'll build a simple greeting component to visualize how we can use props and state within our JSX.
slides.visualDescription: A code block displaying a Greeting component example using props, illustrating live code during the example.

slides.title: Hands-On Practice
slides.content: It's your turn! Write a simple JSX component that takes a 'name' prop and renders a welcoming message. Remember to include proper syntax!
slides.visualDescription: A live coding environment setup suggestion for students to practice writing JSX components and incentivize group collaboration.

slides.title: Quick Recap of JSX
slides.content: Let's summarize what we learned today. JSX simplifies writing HTML in your JavaScript, supports component rendering, and allows dynamic UI creation. Remember: JSX is a powerful tool in your React toolkit!
slides.visualDescription: An infographic summarizing key points of JSX, using bullet points and minimal designs for quick recollection.

slides.title: Feedback and Questions
slides.content: What questions do you have about JSX? Let’s share thoughts and discuss how we can use JSX in our future projects. Please rate your understanding on a scale of 1-5.
slides.visualDescription: A simple feedback chart ready for students to rate their understanding, making it easy to collect responses interactively.
